title: The Bell Rope
text: A shrine's great bell hangs silent over the courtyard, green with age, its rope worn smooth by a thousand hands. A sign is nailed beneath it in six languages: ring once for each prayer, but never more than six. Someone has scratched a seventh line into the wood.

options.label: Ring it once, for the party, and pray for safe passage.

outcomes.text: One clear note rolls out over the courtyard. The way ahead feels lighter, as if something has been listening kindly.

options.label: The devout rings it six times, as the sign says, and not once more.

outcomes.text: Six notes, each deeper than the last, and something listening is pleased.

options.label: Ring it a seventh time, to learn why someone dared to scratch that line.

outcomes.text: The seventh note does not sound. Something hears it anyway, and comes to see who rang, and it is not pleased.
